newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Gold recovers from low, silver to push up.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Gold recovers from low, silver to push up.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
-----------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 17--------------
Gold may continue to recover from a thrust down to $337.50 on Wednesday, but $345-$346 should provide stiff resistance, analysts said.
Silver was looking more buoyant, however, and was likely to press on with attacking resistance around $4.83, they added
GOLD -
The market was recuperating from recent fund attacks which sent prices towards the lows of the year, but it was unclear how much of a bounce could be sustained.
Rumours of central bank selling were dismissed by analyst Larry Kaplan of Flemings Global Mining Group, who believed the downside was limited.
"However, the problem remains when and in what circumstances will investors be sucked back in and generate some sustained price upside," he said.
Analysts at Elliott Wave International said Wednesday's move appeared to be an important low, from which the market should rebound.

"A sound break of resistance in the $342.00 region, that is, current levels, would add confidence that an important low was in and clear the way toward $344.20 and higher. Short-term support is the $340.30-$340.20 area," analyst John Sowden said in a commentary written on Thursday morning.
Other analysts said resistance was expected to be strong at $345-$346, the break out point for the move down, and where the declining 10-day moving average was adding pressure.
Analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff, however, looking at the April Comex contract, was not convinced that prices could march higher.

"Support below $340 is holding, though with the technical indicators remaining weak, further selling pressure may yet be seen. On a confirmed breach of $340, we would then look to target $330," he said.
At 0820 GMT spot gold was quoted at $341.50/342.00, up 20 cents from Wednesday's New York close.
SILVER -
The market was much healthier than gold, having steamed to a high of $4.81 in the spot market on Wednesday.
Squires of Wolff, referring to the Comex May contract, said further challenges of resistance were on the cards.
"A confirmed break of $4.8250 would confirm a double bottom pattern, which has a potential target of $5.00," he said.
On the spot market, prices early on Thursday probed above the recent high of $4.83 hit on April 8, a confirmed break of which would target $4.86 to $4.88, analysts said.
Prices must get a foothold above $4.88, the top of the recent range, to make the market look more positive, they added.
Support was pegged at Wednesday's low of $4.70, down to the recent low of $4.65.
At 0740 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.83/4.85, up four cents from Wednesday's New York close.
PLATINUM -
Prices were on the upswing again, but still rangebound. On the upside, the recent spike high of $374 and trendline resistance around $373 should provide a cap to any movement higher.
Support was pegged at $360.
At 0740 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $369.00/370.00, up $1.00 from Wednesday's New York close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
